starting_state: Illustrative prepared copper-positive group-IIA aliquot before ammonium hydroxide. Pale blue appearance is a rendering assumption requiring sample/source review; no concentration or volume is claimed.
scope: Ammonium-hydroxide stage only. Upstream group separation, later acetic-acid acidification and ferrocyanide confirmation are omitted; do not combine all stages in one shot.

clips.name: ammonia_delivery
clips.action: Slowly deliver ammonium hydroxide into the existing pale-blue copper sample with the tip above the rim, following the source's excess-ammonia condition; preserve headspace and stop delivery.
clips.state_after: The source's transparent deep-blue ammonia complex develops when sufficient excess ammonia and mixing are reached. Do not force a completed endpoint into this brief excerpt or show the later brown ferrocyanide precipitate.

prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Photorealistic landscape16:9 close laboratory starting frame for a copper(II) qualitative-analysis sample before ammonia addition. Exactly one plain transparent upright round-bottom glass test tube secured in a minimal clamp, holding a modest low charge around the lowest quarter of tube height of transparent PALE SKY-BLUE aqueous copper(II) solution. Blue liquid is dilute, clear enough to see the background through it, not dark royal-blue yet, no turbidity, powder, precipitate or separate upper layer. Entire tube, rounded base and open mouth visible, tube70percent image height, abundant headspace for later dropwise reagent delivery. Fixed eye-level view, neutral grey bench/background, even diffuse lighting and realistic restrained glass reflections. No hands, pipette, bottles, extra vessels, text, labels, scale, logos or watermark. An illustrative prepared copper-positive aliquot, not proof of concentration, volume or completed ammonia-complex formation.
